title: AMD vs. Intel | Q3 2026 earnings calls
gist: Comparing Q3 2026 earnings, Intel was still larger but AMD grew more than twice as fast and guided to a higher Q4 revenue midpoint, with both citing strong data-center demand. AMD guides to data centers above 80% of 2027 revenue, while Intel is supply-constrained on Xeon with a PC slowdown through at least 1H27.

insights.claim: In Q3 2026 Intel was still larger than AMD by revenue, but AMD grew more than twice as fast and guided to a higher Q4 revenue midpoint.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AMD continues to close the revenue gap and has stronger near-term momentum.
insights.locator: Intel was still larger in Q3

insights.claim: Both AMD and Intel reported strong data-center demand.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI-driven server demand is lifting both incumbents.

insights.claim: Data-center figures are not strictly comparable because each company uses its own segment definitions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: AMD's growth is increasingly concentrated in data centers, with both EPYC CPUs and Instinct GPUs contributing to a record quarter.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AMD's revenue mix and valuation hinge on data-center AI execution.

insights.claim: AMD management expects data centers to exceed 80% of 2027 revenue, up from roughly 64% this quarter.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A mix shift from ~64% to >80% makes AMD far more exposed to hyperscaler capex cycles.

insights.claim: AMD's combined Client and Gaming segment fell 8% even though client revenue rose 7%, because gaming revenue fell 40%.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Gaming is a sharp drag while client holds up.

insights.claim: AMD's next step is shipping Helios AI racks in volume alongside the ramp of Venice server CPUs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Volume Helios shipments are the key test of AMD's rack-scale AI strategy.
insights.locator: The next step is shipping Helios

insights.claim: AMD management said it expects total revenue to grow more than 80% in 2027, depending on scaling Helios racks and Venice CPUs, with high-bandwidth memory supply a constraint to watch.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The 2027 outlook carries execution and HBM supply risk.

insights.claim: Intel's AI-related demand showed up most clearly in Xeon, with strong server CPU demand and an expanded Oracle collaboration, but manufacturing and packaging constraints limit how fast it can raise shipments.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Intel has unmet demand; the constraint is capacity, not orders.

insights.claim: Intel expects the PC slowdown to last at least through the first half of 2027.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Client weakness persists, offsetting data-center strength.

insights.claim: A factory shutdown in Israel contributes to Intel's projected Q4 margin drop, though its CFO expects little carryover into 2027 margins.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Q4 margin hit is framed as one-time.

insights.claim: Intel expects strong server CPU demand to continue into 2027, with supply tighter in the first half than the second.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Supply relief in 2H27 could unlock deferred Xeon revenue.

insights.claim: The next quarter will test whether AMD can turn early Helios deployments into volume and whether Intel can convert unmet Xeon demand into sales while stabilizing margins.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Defines the key catalysts to watch for both stocks.
